questions.question: Given `function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined`, what is the type of `first(["UPI", "CARD"])`?
questions.explanation: TypeScript infers T from the argument. The array literal is inferred as string[], so T is string and the return type is string | undefined.

questions.question: `function emptyList<T>(): T[] { return []; }` is called as `emptyList()` with no type argument. What is the result type?
questions.explanation: Nothing at the call site mentions T, so inference has no candidates and falls back to unknown, giving unknown[]. Pass a type argument such as emptyList<string>() instead.

questions.question: What is the main problem with `async function fetchJson<T>(url: string): Promise<T> { return (await (await fetch(url)).json()) as T; }`?
options: The cast to T is only an assertion; nothing checks that the response actually matches T
Promise<T> is not a valid return type
T must be constrained to object
questions.explanation: Generics describe types but do not validate data. The server could return any shape and the code would still claim it is T; runtime validation is needed at such boundaries.

questions.question: According to the 'appear at least twice' rule, which signature uses a type parameter pointlessly?
options: function mapArray<T, U>(items: T[], fn: (item: T) => U): U[]
function pair<K, V>(key: K, value: V): [K, V]
questions.explanation: In logValue, T appears only once, so it relates nothing to anything. A plain parameter of type unknown expresses the same thing more simply.
